voices.1: en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural (chosen voice), base rate -8%, directed per passage (render_edge.py)

tracks.room: Anywhere just inside your gate (heard before you reach the start)
tracks.title: Welcome to Park Güell
tracks.where: Play it anywhere just inside the gate you came in by, out of the way of the ticket check; it needs no view. The loop then starts on the entrance esplanade inside the Carrer d'Olot gate, between the two gatehouses.
tracks.what: Park Güell, Eusebi Güell's private garden-city estate on the Carmel hill, by Antoni Gaudí, works begun 1900, a public park since 1926 (aj1 Q3; op4 Q2; F1.9, F1.15, F3.1); the route in the official A–I order with the viaducts first (MAP; PLAN_V2 §1); practical lines (ACCREG 3.23, 2.11; FAQ; RESTRICT; MOB26; COMP); the three lengths (PLAN_V2 §3, Lead's decision 1); the three visitor gates (NODE268, ACCESS; RA M2 text).
tracks.listen: What Park Güell was meant to be, the route through it, the few rules that matter, and how to find the start from any gate.

tracks.room: The entrance esplanade · inside the Carrer d'Olot gate, facing the wall and its medallions
tracks.title: The entrance esplanade — Park with a k
tracks.where: On the entrance esplanade just inside the main gate on Carrer d'Olot, between the two gatehouses, facing the iron gates and the stone wall with its tiled top and name medallions.
tracks.what: The boundary wall of rustic stone with ceramic tiling and "Park Güell" medallions (op6, F5.2); the estate as "a private estate, closed in by a wall, with a porter's service" (es8, E20); the English "Park" (op4, F1.12, Q2); the garden city begun in 1900 (aj3, F1.13); the gardens named after the Font del Carbó, and the tentative start of building around that spring, below Casa Larrard, in 1875 (s3 p. 99 "una tímida urbanització", op24, E111; FA M1: never "the first building on this hillside").
tracks.listen: What the wall and its name tell you about the estate Güell meant to build, before you climb a step.

tracks.room: The Carrer d'Olot gate · just inside, to one side of the palm-leaf iron gates
tracks.title: The Carrer d'Olot gate — A glove shop window
tracks.where: Just inside the main gate on Carrer d'Olot, standing to one side of the palm-leaf iron gates, out of the way of people leaving.
tracks.what: The 1878 glove-shop display case for Esteve Comella (op3, F1.8); Eusebi Güell's family, studies, textile and cement firms, politics and microbiology book (s1, F1.1–F1.6); the Palau Güell (1886) and the park (1900) (op3, F1.9); "a real story of friendship" (op3, Q1); the palm-leaf gates from Casa Vicens (op6, F5.3; no date, F15.38).
tracks.listen: How a glove shop's window began a lifelong partnership, who Güell was, and where the iron gates really came from.

tracks.room: The entrance esplanade · between the two pavilions, both roofs in view
tracks.title: The entrance esplanade — Factory seconds
tracks.where: On the entrance esplanade between the two gatehouses, where both roofs can be seen: the tall tower with its cross on the left as you face the stairway, the other gatehouse on the right.
tracks.what: The two entrance pavilions, the Porter's Lodge pair (op6, F5.4–5.5): the office "with a waiting room and telephone booth", and the caretaker's home, today MUHBA's Casa del Guarda (E1); among the first things built (F5.7 HEDGE); trencadís from factory seconds (s6 p. 26, F5.13) in more than ten whites (s6 p. 26, E100); trencadís history (s24, F15.20); the 1904 plans without the mushroom ventilators (Andruet, G41, G61 HEDGE; E103: no house named); the Hansel and Gretel legend (F5.17 LEGEND, G58, G59 HEDGE; s16 re-read, E60).
tracks.listen: Two gatehouses dressed in factory rejects, mushrooms that came later, and the fairy tale everyone tells about them.

tracks.room: The tower pavilion · outside, its tower and door in view
tracks.title: The tower pavilion — Telephones and a tower
tracks.where: Outside the gatehouse with the tall tower, on the left as you face the stairway, with the tower and its door in view, clear of the doorway and of people passing.
tracks.what: The office pavilion of the Porter's Lodge pair: a visitors' room with telephones in MUHBA's schools story (aj3, E88: fictional register, disclosed); two modest rooms, reception below and office above (s6 p. 20, E96); the tower, about 13 m, a hyperbolic paraboloid of two layers of thin brick tied in a double helix (s6 pp. 20, 22, E97); Gaudí's four-armed cross (s15, F5.9); the original porcelain-clad cross destroyed in 1936, a post-war cross until 1996, today's from photographs of the original (s6 pp. 27–28, E98, C20); the bullseye panes (s6 p. 26, E104).
tracks.listen: A front desk for a gated estate, a tower of thin brick, and a cross that is the third of its line.

tracks.room: Casa del Guarda · outside its door, the gatehouse without the tower
tracks.title: Casa del Guarda — A modest dwelling
tracks.where: Outside the door of the Casa del Guarda, the other gatehouse, the one without the tower, on the right as you face the stairway; stand clear of the doorway and of any queue.
tracks.what: The Casa del Guarda, the caretaker's house, "a modest dwelling" (aj4, F5.6); an elliptical plan with two half-circles (s6 p. 23, F5.11, E13); La Pedrera's "mushroom-shaped dome", in the body only and attributed (s15; E103 HEDGE: s6 p. 23 puts its "sombrero en forma de seta" on the office pavilion; never used to find the house, which is found as the gatehouse without the tower, lead's decision 7 Nov); ground-floor walls 50 cm of stone from the park's old quarries (s6 p. 21, E99); private homes from the 1920s to the 1980s (s6, F5.14); the other pavilion a builders' hut (s6 p. 21, E102); restored at the end of the 1990s (F5.15); a MUHBA branch since 2010 (E1, G-S34); the exhibition and its three floors (aj4, F5.16, DATED).
tracks.listen: The one house on the hill built for a working man, what happened to it after the estate failed, and what the city museum shows inside.

tracks.room: Casa del Guarda · inside, on the ground floor (Extra)
tracks.title: Casa del Guarda · Extra · The caretaker's rooms
tracks.where: Inside the Casa del Guarda, on the ground floor; the first paragraph can be heard as you go in, and the rest standing in the rooms, clear of the stairs.
tracks.what: The caretaker's ground floor: "a small space, designed to be used by a humble family" (aj4, E19); vestibule, kitchen, pantry and living room (s6 p. 20, E12); two parabolic arches in the load-bearing walls, with no catenary gloss (s6 p. 23, E13; FA S8); lime plaster with natural pigments, each room's original colour recovered in the 1996–99 restoration (s6 p. 25, E16, F5.15); the floor's theme, the house, Gaudí's "architectural uniqueness" (es4, E5; DATED).
tracks.listen: What the caretaker's family had downstairs, and how much care went into a house for the humblest people on the estate.

tracks.room: Casa del Guarda · inside, on the first floor (Extra)
tracks.title: Casa del Guarda · Extra · Four bedrooms and a promoter
tracks.where: Inside the Casa del Guarda, on the first floor, standing clear of the stairs.
tracks.what: The first floor as built: four bedrooms and an attic space (s6 p. 20, E12); steel-and-ceramic beams instead of arches (s6 p. 23, E13); the floor's theme, the park (es1, E7; es4; DATED); the curator Mireia Freixa (with Mar Leniz, G80) and her line on the promoter (es1, E3); the museum's visits on Gaudí and Güell, the park and the city (es10, E22).
tracks.listen: The caretaker family's bedrooms, and the exhibition's point about the man who paid for everything.

tracks.room: Casa del Guarda · inside, on the top floor, under the dome (Extra)
tracks.title: Casa del Guarda · Extra · A stair round a chimney
tracks.where: Inside the Casa del Guarda, on the top floor under the dome, where the spiral stair to the lookout can be seen. Do not climb the stair unless it is open to visitors.
tracks.what: The top floor: a spiral stair to the mirador whose inner brick cylinder is both the chimneys' smoke outlet and, with the stair's shaft, the support of the ceramic steps (s6 p. 24, E14); a Catalan dome of three layers of thin brick tied with a twisted metal strap (s6 p. 24, E15); "his use of the Catalan vault" (G-S26); the two attic windows that form crosses of porcelain (s6 p. 27, E16; FA N4); the floor's theme, the city (es4, E8; DATED); the panel "A portrait of monumental Barcelona in 1917" (es4 p. 47; G-S25; DATED).
tracks.listen: A stair held up by its own chimney, a dome of thin brick, and the city the exhibition sets the park in.

tracks.room: The Low Viaduct (Pont de Baix) · on the viaduct, out of the way
tracks.title: The Low Viaduct — Roads before houses
tracks.where: On the Low Viaduct, the Pont de Baix, at the top of the steps and ramps from the Marianao entrance, standing to one side where the plant pots along its railing can be seen.
tracks.what: The roads first, from 1900 (s6 p. 20, F3.3); a 3 km network (op11, F10.1); "all the viaducts, save details" by January 1903 (Andruet, G43); three five-metre viaducts from the Carrer d'Olot side, named on the first postcards (op29, F10.2); sloping columns and vaults of unhewn site stone (op29, F10.3; op11); the hill's stone sold (s3, F2.15); road, shelter and buttress (op12, F10.5); a cistern for each viaduct (op13, F8.6); the pots as railing (op13, F10.8); the 2019–20 recovery of the Low Viaduct's geometry and its railings' three levels of holes (op28, F10.9); the lean that carries the load (version-neutral, G16); the hope that plants would cover the structure (es29, E71).
tracks.listen: Why Gaudí built roads and bridges before any house, what these bridges were for, and what he expected to happen to them.

tracks.room: The Low Viaduct · beside it, its leaning columns seen from the side
tracks.title: The Low Viaduct — Why the columns lean
tracks.where: Beside the Low Viaduct on an open path, where its two rows of leaning stone columns can be seen from the side; keep to the path.
tracks.what: The Low Viaduct's curve on two rows of inclined columns forming a parabola (op13, F10.8); Kopsida's 2011 UPC master's thesis on this viaduct: the viaduct about 50 m long, columns up to 6 m, modelled from the Ajuntament's drawings (not measured by her), the lean's structural meaning, the thrust line inside the vault (G15, G16; FA M2, S1); the same solution later in the crypt of the Colònia Güell (s15, F10.10).
tracks.listen: Why the stone columns under this bridge lean, and where Gaudí used the idea again.

tracks.room: The Low Viaduct · in the shelter under the viaduct
tracks.title: The Low Viaduct — Caves dug for stone
tracks.where: In the covered shelter under the Low Viaduct, among the rough stone columns, standing to one side of anyone passing.
tracks.what: The viaducts "simulate natural caves" (op12); the architects' visit of 4 Jan 1903, Gaudí "en representació del Sr. Güell", Salvador Sellés's memoir "prèviament supervisada per Gaudí" (s3 pp. 102, 104, G50); Bassegoda's Catalan retelling of Sellés on the caves, torchlight, the caves artificial and dug for stone (s3 p. 102, F2.16, G51; FA M2, S2, S3); the fossil cave of 1900 and its Pleistocene animals, now in the natural sciences museum (s3 pp. 100–102; es16, E45); destitute families in the caves after the war (s3 p. 103, E43).
tracks.listen: How a party of architects saw the hill's caves by torchlight in 1903, why the caves were there at all, and what else the diggers found.

tracks.room: The Middle Viaduct (Pont del Mig) · where it comes into view (Extra; if the path is open)
tracks.title: The Middle Viaduct · Extra · The carob bridge
tracks.where: A little higher up the open path from the Low Viaduct, where the Middle Viaduct, the Pont del Mig, comes into view with the carob trunk; do not go on past the works closure.
tracks.what: The Middle Viaduct, "the carob bridge" (op12, F10.7; aj3 caption, V); the farm before the park: vines, olives and orchards, abandoned for poor access, low yields and phylloxera (es16, E48); the carob a survivor of the farm "perhaps" only (RA L4c: MUHBA's vegetation line lives in 031; op12 "natural growth… respected", FA N6: never "bent round"); DATED: the path higher up, to the High Viaduct, closed for works (op24, RA S2; its only home now, RA L4b).
tracks.listen: A road that bends round a tree, and the farm that grew on this hill before the park.

tracks.room: The foot of the stairway · in the queue for the second control (standing; or just before the check if there is no queue)
tracks.title: The foot of the stairway — The healthy quarter
tracks.where: Standing in the queue for the second ticket check, at the foot of the great stairway on the entrance esplanade; if there is no queue, stand to one side just before the check. Nothing to look at until the last paragraph.
tracks.what: The sale of the top of the Muntanya Pelada by the Marquis of Marianao to Eusebi Güell, summer (9 Jul) 1899 (s3, F2.2); La Salut quarter of Gràcia, which Barcelona had absorbed in 1897 (aj3, F2.1 corrected by E68; never "then a separate town"); the 1904 application for Can Muntaner de Dalt and Can Coll i Pujol (G38); the memorandum signed by Güell (s2b, F1.16) with his words on the "barrio de la salud" (G37, V, Lead's decision 5); the plans signed by Güell and Gaudí, 26 Oct 1904 (G39), the permit of 30 Jan 1906 (G40), works begun 1900 (F3.1); MUHBA's water framing (G86, DATED).
tracks.listen: How Güell pitched a bare hill as a healthy suburb for businessmen, in his own signed words, and how long the paperwork lagged behind the digging.

tracks.room: The foot of the stairway · in the queue for the second control (standing; or just before the check if there is no queue)
tracks.title: The foot of the stairway — Sixty plots, two houses
tracks.where: Still in the queue for the second ticket check at the foot of the great stairway, or standing to one side just before it if there is no queue. Nothing to look at until the last paragraph, which carries the one-way warning.
tracks.what: Some 60 triangular plots (op4, F2.9), a sixth buildable (op4, F2.11); services (s6, F2.13); shared services planned (aj3, F2.14; FA N7); more buyers' rules: no industry or anything that disturbed the neighbours, a fee for the shared park's upkeep (E67, MUHBA secondary dossier; E101 optional, cut for length); the 50-peseta tree fine and Güell's approval of plans, in MUHBA's schools story (aj3, F2.12); the sea-view rule only as a forward pointer (036 is its home, RA L1); the first plot to the lawyer Martí Trias (op4, F2.18); the show house (op4, F2.21); two houses (F2.20 safe); transport and the rules (s2b, Q13); works abandoned 1914 (op4, F3.10). One-way warning (RESTRICT).
tracks.listen: The estate on paper: sixty plots, strict rules, and why only two houses were ever built; then the one-way warning before the check.

tracks.room: The Dragon Stairway · at the foot, past the control, the first flight and the grottos in view
tracks.title: The Dragon Stairway — A bus shelter before buses
tracks.where: At the foot of the Dragon Stairway, just past the second ticket check, to one side where the first flight, its battlemented side walls, the grottos beneath them and the first landing can be seen.
tracks.what: The twin stairway in three flights between walls with merlons over two grottos, one a waiting shelter on a conical central column, with fountain water running down (op7, F6.1–F6.3; FLYER, F6.2); "capricious shapes like goblins" on the first landing (op7, F6.4); the op7 description paraphrased, without quotation marks (RA L1); "Monumental Staircase" no longer spoken (op27, FA N4); the first basin cleaned and its trencadís recovered, 2020–21 (op27, F6.13). Which grotto is the shelter is not spoken (O14).
tracks.listen: A grand double stair with a waiting room built into its walls and goblins on its first landing.

tracks.room: The Dragon Stairway · halfway up, beside the coat of arms, out of the way
tracks.title: The Dragon Stairway — A flag on the stairs
tracks.where: Halfway up the Dragon Stairway, to one side of the steps, beside the red and yellow stripes of the Catalan coat of arms with a snake's head above them; the dragon is just above.
tracks.what: The serpent-head spout over the coat of arms of Catalonia (FLYER, F6.5; op7 "the emblem of Catalonia" halfway up); Güell president of the Centre Català and, in 1900, of the Jocs Florals (s1, F1.5–F1.6); works begun in 1900 (F3.1); García Ávila 2023 on the two men as Catalanists (s20, G25, V); the Catalanist reading in FACTS's hedge (F12.1). No sardanas (033), no count of shields (O14).
tracks.listen: Why Catalonia's coat of arms sits halfway up a garden stair, and what it says about the man who paid for it.

tracks.room: The Dragon Stairway · beside the dragon
tracks.title: The Dragon Stairway — The dragon is a drain
tracks.where: Halfway up the Dragon Stairway, beside the creature in broken tile, in a spot where you are not blocking the steps.
tracks.what: The dragon, or salamander, in trencadís (op7, F6.6); the fountain fed from the tank under the Hypostyle Room, the mouth its overflow (op7, op8, s7b; F6.8, F6.9); version-neutral: the coat of arms under a serpent's head (FLYER, F6.5) and Delphi, attributed to "some writers" with Bassegoda named (F12.3 HEDGE, F12.11; s22; FA ed2 N7); the Feb 2007 vandalism (s17, F6.11); separately, the front right foot studied from 2025 by the sculptor Abel Vallhonesta and put back, finished 22 Apr 2026 (op25, F6.12, FA S12, DATED); Vicky Cristina Barcelona (E78, optional, used). Callback 015 (the market up the stairway; safe).
tracks.listen: The city's most famous dragon turns out to be the overflow of a rain tank, with a mended foot and a film role.

tracks.room: The Dragon Stairway · a few steps above the dragon, to the side, looking back down at it
tracks.title: The Dragon Stairway — Lizard, dragon or salamander?
tracks.where: A few steps above the dragon on the Dragon Stairway, standing to the side out of the way of the steps, looking back down at the creature.
tracks.what: Bayard Brattstrom's 2015 letter to the New York Review of Books and Martin Filler's reply (s18, Q8, Q9, F6.14, FA N5); Bassegoda's reading of Gaudí's dragons as Güell's ideas: Catalanism, mythology and religion (s22, Q7, F12.2; re-read 7 Nov 2026, inside quotation marks in an English press note); nearly four hundred dragons in Barcelona, on buildings, fountains and parks, by one photographer's count (s22 "almost four hundred", F6.15 HEDGE; FA ed2 N8). No crocodile of Nîmes (G66), no Delphi (020).
tracks.listen: A zoologist, a critic and a Gaudí scholar each give the creature a different name, and none of them is wrong to try.

tracks.room: The Dragon Stairway · at the top, by the odeon bench and the tripod
tracks.title: The Dragon Stairway — Delphi?
tracks.where: At the top of the Dragon Stairway, on the last flight that runs in under the hall of columns, by the curved stone bench shaped like a little Greek theatre; the tripod of snakes is nearby.
tracks.what: The odeon (Greek-theatre bench) under the Hypostyle Room and the tripod "of three snakes" (op7, FLYER; F6.7, F6.10); the Delphi reading (F12.3 HEDGE): Python, the tripod, a Doric temple; Bassegoda as reported in English (s22, Q6, now confirmed inside quotation marks); García Ávila 2023, "several authors", "above all commercial", his suggestion that a first plan may have followed the temple of Apollo at Cyrene (s20; F12.3, F12.4; G22; FA N6); Gaudí never explained it (F12.11). Carandell not named (Lead's decision 6). Callback 018 (safe).
tracks.listen: A tripod, a dragon and a Doric hall add up to Delphi for some writers; one scholar disagrees, and Gaudí never said.

tracks.room: The Hypostyle Room · outside, at the top of the stairway, the front columns in view (official D)
tracks.title: The Hypostyle Room — A market hall in Greek dress
tracks.where: Outside the Hypostyle Room, at the top of the Dragon Stairway, where you can see the hall's outer row of fat, fluted columns; official stop D.
tracks.what: The Hypostyle Room (Sala Hipòstila), Gaudí, finished in the park's busiest building years (F7.12 HEDGE, no year): the estate's planned market (op8; F7.1, no frequency); 86 fluted Doric-inspired columns (op8, FLYER; F7.2; F15.15 corrected once): the home of the count (RA L15); about six metres, thick for their height (s20; F7.6 HEDGE; FA N8); the outer row leaning against the classical rules, like buttresses (op8, s20; F7.5); the 1986 report on settlement at the front (s20; F7.20); the long restoration of the late 1980s and early 1990s (E77, C7, dates HEDGE). Callback 015 (shared services; safe, FA N7).
tracks.listen: The temple at the top of the stairs was meant to be a market, and its front row breaks the Greek rules by leaning in.

tracks.room: The Hypostyle Room · inside, among the columns, a wide aisle in view (official E)
tracks.title: The Hypostyle Room — Columns that are drainpipes
tracks.where: Inside the Hypostyle Room, among the columns, where you can see down one of the wider aisles where columns were left out; official stop E.
tracks.what: How the columns were made: moulds, lime-mortar concrete with rubble and stones, a wooden roller pulled out to leave a drain to the cistern (s20; F7.9); version-neutral recap of the 86 leaning columns (F7.2, F7.5; RA L15); the rain's route through the square's sandy surface and down the columns (s15, F8.2; FA S4: no domes' hollows); the conduit along the front where the bench sits on the colonnade (op8, F8.1; FA S5); the tank for the park and the houses (s7a; F8.3); the dragon as overflow (callback 018, safe); Bassegoda on the cistern (s4; Q10; F8.5), not open to visitors; DATED: the 2026 plan to restore Gaudí's two rain tanks (F8.10, E86); "three naves" (op8; F7.8); white trencadís at the column feet (s20; F7.10). No capacity (G1, G2); no hatch (O15, G65).
tracks.listen: Every column in this Greek hall was cast round a wooden roller, and the hole it left carries the rain down to a tank below.

tracks.room: The Hypostyle Room · inside, under the small domes of the ceiling, away from the big discs
tracks.title: The Hypostyle Room — The young man on the ceiling
tracks.where: Inside the Hypostyle Room, standing under one of the small domes of the ceiling, away from the four big round discs, looking up.
tracks.what: Josep Maria Jujol (Tarragona 1879 – 1949), twenty-seven years younger than Gaudí (our arithmetic, 1852/1879); full collaboration with Gaudí 1904–1914 (s11, F4.1–F4.2; paraphrased, Duch not re-checked); the ceiling of small clay-brick domes by Gaudí, its tile-shard mosaics by Jujol (op8, FLYER, F7.13); the archive's credit for the bench's trencadís and the hall's panels, "with recycled material" (s10, F4.3); Jujol's son's line, paraphrased (s11, Q5, F4.5); Casa Milà: interior decoration and the running of the site (s10, F4.6, FA S10). No Suns (024); no Jujol quotation (G48).
tracks.listen: The colour over your head is not Gaudí's but his young assistant's, Josep Maria Jujol, and Gaudí trusted him more and more.

tracks.room: The Hypostyle Room · inside, under one of the four big round discs
tracks.title: The Hypostyle Room — Four seasons in glass
tracks.where: Inside the Hypostyle Room, standing under one of the four big round discs in the ceiling, looking up.
tracks.what: The four Suns, one for each season, as the city reads them (aj8; Q11; F7.14); version-neutral credit to Josep Maria Jujol (F4.3); the glassware in them (aj8; F7.16); the 2013 emergency, each Sun cut into 24 pieces, taken down, restored and put back, with no year spoken (aj8 gives none; F7.18's "2016" is only the press note's footer: FA ed2 S5, RC), by the restorers Gamarra & García with Eurocatalana (F4.15). No moon reading, no count of small discs (G8, G9); no dolls' heads or plates (F7.17). Cue: the Font Sarva Extra, then the one-way route up the hall's right-hand side to the Austria Gardens (RA M1, RA S3).
tracks.listen: The four great discs overhead are suns for the seasons, made from the glassware of somebody's dining table.

tracks.room: The Font Sarva · at its little room beside the Hypostyle Room (Extra; if open)
tracks.title: The Font Sarva · Extra · Güell's bottled water
tracks.where: At the door of the Font Sarva's small room, set in the enclosing wall of the Hypostyle Room; play it only if the room is open, and step back into the one-way flow afterwards.
tracks.what: The Font Sarva, a spring older than the park, hidden in the basement of the Hypostyle Room and fed by mine water from the hill (s19; F8.7); placed "in the enclosing wall" of the hall (G65); La Salut neighbours with jugs; water piped down to the old Larrard farmhouse (s19 "també es canalitza fins a la deu de l'antiga masia Larrard"; F8.9; FA N9, FA ed2 S6; lead's decision 7 Nov: the receiving point is not called a well or a spring); Güell's 1913 analysis, magnesium, bottled and sold as medicinal water in chemists' shops for about a decade (s19; F8.7); its room opened up in the works ending 2020 (op23; F3.28); DATED: visitable since September 2020 (s19; F8.8), now implied by op23's words only (cut for the X cap).
tracks.listen: A spring older than the park, which Güell tried to sell in chemists' shops, and which spent decades hidden in the hall's basement.

tracks.room: The Austria Gardens · just inside the gardens
tracks.title: The Austria Gardens — An empty plot
tracks.where: Just inside the Austria Gardens, the terraced gardens you reach by the one-way route up the Hypostyle Room's right-hand side; stand to one side of the path, with the flower beds in view.
tracks.what: The Austria Gardens (Jardins d'Àustria): a zone of estate plots (op14; F11.2), then the municipal plant nursery after the park became public (op14; E81); named after a donation of trees from Austria in 1977 (op14; F11.1; C1: never "the Austrian government" in our voice); many of the donated high-altitude trees died, and in 2012 the lawns were replaced with flowering and aromatic plants (es16; E57; DATED, O26); "a completely different look to the rest of the park" (op14; E105); from the centre, the two houses built in Güell's time (op14; F11.3). Callback 015 (the sixty plots; safe).
tracks.listen: A garden that was meant to be a building plot, how it got its name, and why the beds you see are younger than the name.

tracks.room: The Austria Gardens · near the middle, Casa Trias in view among the trees
tracks.title: The Austria Gardens — The first buyer
tracks.where: Near the middle of the Austria Gardens, where you can see across them to the houses among the trees above; Casa Trias is a private home, seen from here only.
tracks.what: Casa Trias: the plot sold to the lawyer Martí Trias i Domènech on 24 July 1902 (s3; F2.18), the estate's first buyer, "a friend of Güell" (op4); house by Juli Batllevell, 1903–1906 (op17; F2.19), "true to the style of his master" Domènech i Montaner (es27; E66); the lawyer and his wife Anna Maxenchs lived there in the first half of the twentieth century (es27; E66; C2); still a private residence owned by the same family (op17; F2.19); DATED: the city's compulsory purchase (G29); the works closure beyond Casa Trias is not spoken here: its one home is 013 (op24; F3.31; RA ed2 L4b). Callback 015 (Trias's plot; safe).
tracks.listen: The estate's first buyer was Güell's own lawyer, and his house is still in his family's hands.

tracks.room: The Austria Gardens · the pink house with the pointed tower in view
tracks.title: The Austria Gardens — The house Gaudí didn't design
tracks.where: In the Austria Gardens, near their middle, where the pink house with the pointed tower, the Gaudí House Museum, can be seen among the trees; outside only.
tracks.what: The estate's show house, now the Gaudí House Museum (Casa Museu Gaudí): put up by the works contractor Josep Pardo i Casanovas as a model home, to the plans of Francesc Berenguer i Mestres, signed by Gaudí because Berenguer had no architect's title (op16, op4, op22, s3; F2.21, F2.23, F4.8); "a few years into the works" (F2.22 HEDGE); bought by the Gaudí family in 1906 (F2.24 HEDGE); Gaudí there for nearly twenty years, until 1925 (G79; version-neutral for E); the Chiappos and "Casa Gaudí"; opened as a museum in 1963 thanks to the Friends of Gaudí (op22, op4; F11.11, F3.19, E80; FA N10); iron railings from Casa Vicens and Casa Milà in its garden, self-contained Casa Vicens clause (op22; F11.12); pink stucco walls, pointed tower (op22). F15.3 / F11.13 corrected once. Callback 015 (the show house; safe).
tracks.listen: Gaudí's home for nearly twenty years was a show house drawn by his right-hand man, Berenguer, with Gaudí's signature on the plans.

tracks.room: The Austria Gardens · the pink house still in view
tracks.title: The Austria Gardens — A father and a niece
tracks.where: The same spot in the Austria Gardens, with the pink house with the pointed tower still in view among the trees; outside only.
tracks.what: Gaudí moved into the show house in 1906 with his father, Francesc Gaudí i Serra, and his niece Rosa, known as Roseta, daughter of his sister Rosa, brought up by her grandfather and uncle from early childhood (op4, op22; F3.6, F11.7; E65; C9); his father died in October 1906, his niece in 1912 (op22; F11.8; FA S9); Gaudí there "almost twenty years, from 1906 until a few months before his death" (G79); he left in November 1925 for a small study at the Sagrada Família (es25; E63; C8); partly, it is said, to be near the ailing sculptor Llorenç Matamala (es26; E64 HEDGE, single source). No causes of death; nothing on the niece's father (E65).
tracks.listen: Who shared Gaudí's house on this hill, how soon he was left alone in it, and why he finally went down to the Sagrada Família.

tracks.room: The Austria Gardens · a terrace with the city below in view
tracks.title: The Austria Gardens — Down the hill every morning
tracks.where: On a terrace higher up the Austria Gardens, along the one-way route, where the city below comes into view; stand to one side of the path.
tracks.what: Gaudí's daily round in his park years, as the Sagrada Família's own blog describes it: down to the parish church of Sant Joan de Gràcia; after mass on to the Sagrada Família (commissioned 1883); in the evening to Sant Felip Neri for prayer and vespers; back up "on foot or by tram", with the evening edition of La Veu de Catalunya under his arm; "between eight and ten kilometres a day" (es25; E62; DATED: re-check the blog before recording). The gardens' "good views" (op14; E105). No landmark named (O7 not done).
tracks.listen: How Gaudí spent his days while he lived on this hill: down to the city in the morning, and back up in the evening.

tracks.room: The Austria Gardens · on the upper path, among the trees
tracks.title: The Austria Gardens — A Mediterranean garden
tracks.where: On the upper path along the top of the Austria Gardens, among the trees, out of the way of the one-way flow; the Nature Square lies ahead along this path.
tracks.what: Josep Maria Montserrat, director of the Barcelona Botanic Garden, talk of 10 Feb 2011: the park as "the last modernist garden, and one of the first Mediterranean gardens in Barcelona"; beyond the square, the aim to keep the "pre-existing agricultural landscape", mainly carob and olive (es19; E58); MUHBA's guide: Gaudí respected the existing vegetation and planted Mediterranean species (es8; E59); MUHBA's schools story: Güell had the hill replanted with pines, holm oaks, palms and olives (aj3; E89, labelled as the story); the 2009 wind and 2010 snow, and the switch to native, low-water species (es16; E56); twenty-five bird species on the operator's list, among them the hoopoe (es16; E52). No tree species pointed out (O26 not done); no parrots (E53).
tracks.listen: Why a botanist called this the last modernist garden and one of Barcelona's first Mediterranean ones, and what still grows and sings here.

tracks.room: The Nature Square · out in the open, away from the edge
tracks.title: The Nature Square — You're standing on the roof
tracks.where: Out in the open middle of the Nature Square, the great sandy square on top of the hall of columns, away from the tiled bench and the edge; stand where you can also see the long stone retaining wall against the hill.
tracks.what: The Nature Square (Plaça de la Natura, the Greek Theatre of the first plans): artificial, part dug into the rock, part held up on the Hypostyle Room; planned for large open-air shows watched from the terraces around it (op9; F9.1–9.3); its sandy surface as the start of the rain's route, as a callback to 022 only (F8.2; the La Pedrera line lives in 022, RA ed2 L3e); waterproofing and the link to the cistern redone 2017–2019 (op31; F9.18b); a 2008 UPC doctoral thesis argues the park is a rainwater receiver built against erosion, with no document to prove it (G4); the retaining wall's palm-tree capitals (op9; F9.6). No view, no sea rule (036); no parties (033); no "eighty-six" (021).
tracks.listen: Why the great square is really a roof, a theatre and a rain catcher, and the thesis that the whole park is a rain machine.

tracks.room: The Nature Square · out in the open
tracks.title: The Nature Square — Garden parties
tracks.where: The same open spot in the middle of the Nature Square, away from the bench and the edge.
tracks.what: The Garden Party of the first international congress of the Catalan language, October 1906 (no day: C4; G75 gives 20 Oct, MUHBA's photo caption 14 Oct, E61), called that in English, held as part of the congress (FA M3), photographed by Frederic Ballell (E61); Güell's aim to promote his estate (G76; FA N11); events in the square by 1907 (op4; F3.7); Catalanist events and sardanas, "one of Barcelona's great tourist attractions" in Güell's lifetime (op3; F9.4; RA L16: their only home); the 1 May 1908 charity race from the Carrer d'Olot gate to the top of the Turó de les Tres Creus (s3; G53); DATED: the invitation to the centenary community dinner for April 2026 (s9, 9 Jan 2026; F3.32; FA ed2 N14: no report found that it took place, so only the invitation is spoken; RC).
tracks.listen: How the estate's square became a stage for parties, dances and even a race, and why every party was also a sales pitch.

tracks.room: The Nature Square · at the bench (sit if you can)
tracks.title: The Nature Square — A hundred metres of broken tile
tracks.where: At the long tiled bench that runs along the edge of the Nature Square on the stairway side; sit if there's room, or stand beside it without crowding the people sitting.
tracks.what: The undulating bench of the Nature Square, built 1909–1914, finished 1914 (op4, FLYER; F3.9, F9.8): balustrade and water collector (op9, F9.7; G69); the whole square the roof of the hall of columns (op9; version-neutral for H; RA ed2 R3: true sitting or standing); Gaudí shaped it, Jujol's trencadís skin (F4.3, F4.4 safe wording; RA L6, RA N17; callback 024); about a hundred metres by the conservators' measure (s14; F9.9, G62); prefabricated modules (s15; F9.10); Jujol's incisions on the backrest's top and along a line halfway up (s4; F9.15); Marian inscriptions (G49); inner face ceramic and porcelain, outer face glass (s14; F9.14); the wet-plaster legend, once (F9.12, F15.24, s30); the backrest's curve (s15; F9.11 HEDGE wording); conservation since around 1990, backrests photographed one by one (s14, op28; F9.17).
tracks.listen: How a bench became a railing and a drain, who made its colour, and the story about it that nobody has ever proved.

tracks.room: The Nature Square · at the bench (Extra)
tracks.title: The Nature Square · Extra · Words in the tiles
tracks.where: At the tiled bench along the edge of the Nature Square, sitting if there's room, ideally near the rounded top of the backrest where marks are scratched into the tile.
tracks.what: Jujol's Marian inscriptions on the bench, their meaning "still argued over" (s21 calls it an enigma and offers its own answer, so never "an open question" in one study: FA ed2 S2; G49 corrected); Jujol's habit of crosses, Latin phrases, Marian invocations and psalms (s11; G47, his work in general; paraphrased: Duch blocked); the 1986 writings (G7) no longer spoken (RA ed2 N17); the restoration of the late 1980s and early 1990s (C7; E77; G13, G20): coping pieces with an original design probably by Jujol, inscriptions and symbols left out of the new tiles, each new piece engraved with the year it was made (E77; the year itself held until O16), new ceramics by Toni Cumella, the architects' "very precarious"; the 2016 dispute over how much is original and the city's reply (G63, G64; FA N12).
tracks.listen: The prayers Jujol hid in the bench, the restorers who refused to fake them, and the argument over how much of it is original.

tracks.room: The Nature Square · at the bench, looking out over the city
tracks.title: The Nature Square — The view
tracks.where: At the long tiled bench on the stairway side of the Nature Square, looking out over the city; find a gap where you're not leaning over people sitting.
tracks.what: The view from the bench, home of the sea-view rule and the bald hill (RA L1): the site "with almost no vegetation" (aj9, F14.11; FA N15 "Most of the green"); Barcelona of 1900, "over half a million inhabitants" (op2, F1.19); Gràcia joined to Barcelona in 1897 (es29, E68); the rule on the houses' height and placing to protect the view of the sea (op4, FA S6; es29 and es38 add the sunlight, E27, E83, C12); the square as "A viewpoint over the city" (op5, F9.19) and, in MUHBA's schools story, a place "to take the fresh air and watch the city" (aj3, E90, labelled as the story); Turespaña's "best views" of the park and the sea (es11, E24; FA ed2 N15: said of the park; the sea sentence cuttable, O7); the Olympic Village towers (es44, E113: one cuttable paragraph, O7 only, Lead's decision 6; RA ed2 M3); where the rich went instead (es29, E68; poor transport F2.26).
tracks.listen: Why the view from this bench was protected by the estate's rules, and why the buyers it was protected for never came.

tracks.room: The Nature Square · at the bench, the hilltop in view
tracks.title: The Nature Square — Three crosses instead of a chapel
tracks.where: Still at the tiled bench on the Nature Square, with the hill above the park and the three crosses on its top in view.
tracks.what: The Turó de les Tres Creus, the park's highest point, about 180 m (op30, F14.9; never 210 m, E32), once "Ore Hill or the Hill of Mines and Caves" (op30); the estate's chapel, "Capelya" on the plan of the 1903 visit (G42, Andruet), lobed like a six-petalled flower about 30 m across (s3, E38); Bonaventura Bassegoda in the Diario de Barcelona, 1903, in indirect speech (s3, G52; FA M1, RA L7); the chapel never built and the Calvary instead (s3 "s'hagué d'abandonar la construcció de la capella", F12.7; FA ed2 S7: never "never begun"), "which simulated the Calvary" (op30), finished by 1905 (s3, F3.5), eighteen symbolic steps, the middle cross 2 m (s3, E40); destroyed July 1936, rebuilt after the war, not exactly as before (s3, E41, C10); Gaudí's glazed window and the hill he "wanted always to have in view" (s3, E42, C5). Callback to the pink house (028: in E and F).
tracks.listen: The chapel Gaudí planned for the hilltop, the three crosses that took its place, and the hill he kept in view from his window.

tracks.room: The path above Casa Larrard · among the pines, just past the iron door (official H)
tracks.title: The path above Casa Larrard — Two thousand pines
tracks.where: On the path just past the old iron door at the corner of the Nature Square, among the pines above Casa Larrard; step to the edge so the one-way flow can pass.
tracks.what: The trees and the war (the war's one home, PLAN §3): almost all the park's trees cut for firewood during the Civil War, two thousand conifers and other trees planted after it (s3, E43; never "hungry winters"; "much of the park's pinewood", never "these pines"); the path above Casa Larrard through a pine grove, leading on toward his home (op10, F10.13; the iron door is told in 037's cue only, RA ed2 L4f; FA ed2 N18); Storm Glòria, 2020: two old trees down near the Portico, the ceramic roof of the water mine to Casa Larrard broken, the paving restored June–August 2022 (WORKS10, F10.17).
tracks.listen: How a war nearly stripped this hill of its trees, how the pines came back, and what a storm did to two old trees beside the path.

tracks.room: The Portico of the Washerwoman · under the wave, to one side
tracks.title: The Portico of the Washerwoman — The wave
tracks.where: Under the stone portico shaped like a breaking wave, on the path through the pines beyond the Nature Square's iron door; stand to one side so the one-way flow can pass.
tracks.what: The Portico of the Washerwoman (Pòrtic de la Bugadera; the Laundry Room Portico on the park's pages): "a great wave atop slanting columns", "a double colonnade that acts as a buttress" against "a retaining wall made from unworked stone" (op10, F10.13); the flyer's "pedra sense treballar" and "el perfil d'una gran onada" (FLYER CA); "one of the finest examples of the organic architecture upheld by Gaudí" (op10, F10.14, attributed); version-neutral: the name from one column carved as a washerwoman (FLYER, F10.15; H and E skip 040); FA S11 / RA S8: "It stands on leaning columns, as Gaudí's road bridges in the park do" (self-contained, no callback).
tracks.listen: How a wave of rough stone holds up a hillside, and where the portico gets its name.

tracks.room: The Portico of the Washerwoman · beside the washerwoman column, out of the flow
tracks.title: The Portico of the Washerwoman — A washerwoman and two pillars
tracks.where: Beside the column carved as a woman, along the Portico of the Washerwoman; stand to one side, out of the one-way flow.
tracks.what: The washerwoman column: a caryatid that "represents a washerwoman" and "carries the tools of her trade" (FLYER CA, F10.15; what she carries left to the listener's eye until O17); no sculptor named (G72); one researcher's Temple of Jerusalem thesis, 2020 (Rius Santamaria, Matèria 16–17: the park's central area, never "the whole park", FA ed2 S3), with Jachin and Boaz looked for "in this portico" (s21, F10.16, F12.5: LEGEND, "one researcher"; not "the end columns": the paper's p. 172 rejects them, ed1 notes decision 3). NOT: "Masonic", "offering bearer", the mason legend.
tracks.listen: Who the washerwoman is, and one researcher's theory that this portico holds the pillars of Solomon's temple.

tracks.room: Casa Larrard · at the foot of the spiral ramp, the house in view (outside only) (official I)
tracks.title: Casa Larrard — Güell's farmhouse
tracks.where: On the path at the foot of the spiral ramp, with the old farmhouse of Casa Larrard, now the Baldiri Reixac school, in view; stay on the path and out of the school's way.
tracks.what: Casa Larrard, "the stately farmhouse of the old Can Muntaner de Dalt estate" (op15, F2.4); the Larrard family, "a rich family of French origin, made rich by trade and banking", who sold to the Marquis of Marianao (s3, F2.5; callback 014, in E and F; FA S3 past tense); Güell's palace in the old city, built by Gaudí (op3, F1.9; G76); why he left it in 1907: the decayed streets and a situation "molt tensa" (es38, E82, C6; never "violent"); the farmhouse adapted for him by Gaudí (s3 "arranjada per Gaudí", C19; never "rebuilt"); "lived there until his death" (op15); Güell died in this house on 9 July 1918 (s1, op4, F3.11); Gaudí in the show house from 1906 (op4, F3.6; callback 028, in E and F). Outside only: a working school.
tracks.listen: Why the man who paid for the whole estate left his palace and lived out his life in an old farmhouse on his own hill.

tracks.room: Casa Larrard · a few steps on, the house still in view
tracks.title: Casa Larrard — A palace for a king
tracks.where: A few steps on along the path below the spiral ramp, with Casa Larrard still in view; out of the way of the school and the one-way flow.
tracks.what: After Güell's death the heirs offered the park, with their Pedralbes estate, to King Alfonso the Thirteenth as a site for a royal palace; "in 1921 the king chose Pedralbes" (s2a, F3.12; RA L14); the heirs' offer to the city (G77, FA N16, attributed); the city's long purchase: plenary of 26 May 1922, complete by 1925 (op4, s9, s2a, F3.13 HEDGE); Nicolau Maria Rubió i Tudurí, parks director, "the inventor of green Barcelona" in an Ara column (s34, F13.12; FA S7 wording); the farmhouse a municipal school in 1931, named after Baldiri Reixac (op15, F3.16); Reixac (1703–1781), priest and pedagogue, education to begin in the mother tongue and not in Latin (es39, E84).
tracks.listen: How the estate nearly became a royal palace, how the city bought it instead, and whose name the farmhouse school carries.

tracks.room: The way out · walking down past the bandstand and along the wall to the gate (heard walking)
tracks.title: The way out — Six weeks
tracks.where: Heard while walking down from Casa Larrard, past a small round bandstand and along the inside of the wall to the main gate on Carrer d'Olot; keep walking at your own pace and watch your step.
tracks.what: Version-neutral: the city bought the park from Güell's heirs in the early 1920s (F3.13 safe wording; E skips 042); opened as a municipal park on 26 April 1926 (op4, s9, F3.15); "open to all the city's people" (G77 sense of "accés lliure per als ciutadans"; RA S9, never "free access"); Gaudí hit by a tram on 7 June 1926 at Bailèn and the Gran Via, died three days later at the Hospital de la Santa Creu (s31, s32, F13.2, F13.3); he had moved out the year before into his workshop at the Sagrada Família (op16, op22, F3.17; callback 028, in E and F); Dalí's lecture in the park, 1956, filmed (s33, E110, FA-verified Dalí Foundation record; never "newsreels", never what he said); monument 1969 (op1, op4); UNESCO 1984, one of seven Gaudí works on the list (op1, F13.4); DATED: Gaudí Year 2026 (s26, F13.7: cut after 31 Dec 2026).
tracks.listen: How the failed estate opened to the whole city in April 1926, and lost its maker six weeks later.

tracks.room: The Carrer d'Olot gate · just inside, out of the flow
tracks.title: The Carrer d'Olot gate — The neighbours' park
tracks.where: Just inside the main gate on Carrer d'Olot, to one side, out of the way of people leaving.
tracks.what: About nine million visits a year to the heart of the park, estimated in 2012 (aj8, F14.1); "regulated since 2013 to prevent tourist overcrowding" (op19, F3.26); one of the operator's two aims, "an urban park, a place for the community" (op18, FA N18); charging from Friday 25 October 2013 after neighbours complained of the crowds (es30, E72); the neighbourhood associations' manifesto against closing the park, undated and so untied from 2013 ("At one point": es32, E74; FA ed2 S4); "the iguana", 2015, Salvador Barrau of the Coll-Vallcarca residents' association (es31, E73, E112; callback 018, in all); DATED, one sentence each: the controls over all twelve hectares since 2020 (op18, op21, F3.27), free entry for neighbours (op18, F14.5), the 2025 figures (op21, F14.3, FA N18: "free visits"); works funded by the regulation's return (op23, F14.7, no sums); callback only to the Suns, the backrests and the dragon's foot (RA L4; 024, 034, 018 are in Full); "glue Gaudí back together" (F4.15). E75 out (Lead's decision 9); E76 not used (see notes).
tracks.listen: How the estate nobody bought became so crowded that the city had to start counting, and what the neighbours made of it.

tracks.room: The Carrer d'Olot gate · just inside, the stairway in view
tracks.title: The Carrer d'Olot gate — A failed estate
tracks.where: Just inside the main gate on Carrer d'Olot, out of the way of people leaving, with the great stairway in view.
tracks.what: Close. A failed housing estate that became a triumph of a park (F15.2 safe wording): sixty plots, two houses (op4, F2.25). Version-neutral recap (RA L3, 43 words; H skips 041–043): Güell in Casa Larrard until his death in 1918 (op4, op15, F3.11); the city's purchase from his heirs and the opening in April 1926 (F3.13, F3.15); Gaudí's death that June (s31, F13.2). MUHBA: "a perfect symbiosis between urban planning, architecture and nature" (aj1, Q12, F1.17). The people: Jujol's colour on the bench and the ceiling (s10, F4.3, F4.4 safe wording), Berenguer, Gaudí's "right hand", drew the show house (op16, op22, F2.21, F4.7), the builders, an uncle and his nephew, not named in speech (s3, F4.11; RA ed2 L9), the caretaker (aj4, F5.6; no roof identifier, lead's note 7 Nov), the lawyer Martí Trias, first buyer (op4, F2.18; callback 015, in all). Callback 002: Park with a k (op4, F1.12). Goodbye: the Carrer d'Olot gate is the way out; no re-entry (FAQ). Cut: "In 2026 it turned a hundred" (RA N13).
tracks.listen: The whole story in one breath: the estate that failed, the people who made it, and the park it became.
